parsed.why: State-level anti-discrimination, hate-crime and panic-defence laws are documented and enforced (2026 civil-rights ruling), but second-highest incident count, care bans, surgical birth-certificate barrier and 'least safe in region' label pull it below protective divisions; national document regime applies.

Shield law reaching visitors' families, 1993 gender-identity protections, hate-crime coverage, open ID markers and a most-protective-tier ranking; only dated custody-by-birth-sex record weighs down. Strong documented protective machinery lifts it well above the 0.35 national line.

Universal-exposure tier-1 feature: criminalised restroom use in government buildings AND all public-facing private businesses, misdemeanour up to a year, in force July 2026. Plus birth-certificate ban, sports bans, parent-disclosure rule. Adds hostile layer below parent's 0.35.

No facility restriction, statewide gender-identity protections, hate-crime enhancements, panic-defence repeal, court-protected bathroom use, gender-identity prison placement, low-risk assessment. Sports capitulation and failed sanctuary bill are the only drags; national document regime remains.

Fifteen-member 'Most Protective' tier, X markers on licences and birth certificates since 2017, shield law for out-of-state care seekers, hate-crime and panic-defence bans, uniform public-accommodation coverage. Only statutory-not-enforcement caveat and federal sports probe hold it below higher marks.
